The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning. Where other terms or words require definition, please refer to the 1987 U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Wetlands Manual or call the District Corps office in Savannah, at 1-800-448-2402.
Functions means the beneficial roles that wetlands serve, including storage, conveyance and attenuation of floodgate and stormwater; protection of water quantity and quality and reduction of erosion; habit for wildlife, including rare, threatened and endangered species; food chain support for a wide variety of wildlife and fisheries; educational, historical and archeological value protection; and scenic, aesthetic and recreational amenities.
Generalized wetland map means wetlands identified on the U.S. Department of the Interior, Fish and Wildlife Service, National Wetlands Inventory maps.
Hydric soils means soils that form as a result of saturated soil conditions. A list of these soils is maintained by the Natural Resources Conservation Service.
Hydrophytic vegetation means macrophytic plants tolerant of or dependent on saturated soil conditions.
Jurisdictional determination means an official, written statement or map signed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or, in the case of coastal marshlands, the state department of natural resources.
Jurisdictional wetland means a wetland area that meets the definitional requirements for wetlands as determined by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
Regulated activity means any activity which will, or which may reasonably be expected to, result in the discharge of dredged or fill material into waters of the United States excepting those activities exempted in section 18-139 and exempted in section 404 of the Federal Clean Water Act.
Silviculture means the art of producing, reproducing and growing a forest of distinctive stands of trees.
Temporary emergency permit means a temporary permit that may be issued in certain circumstances specified in section 18-141.
Wetland means an area that is inundated or saturated by surface water or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and under normal circumstances does support, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions, commonly known as hydrophytic vegetation. Wetlands generally include swamps, marshes, bogs and similar areas.
Wetland delineation means the establishment of wetland boundaries by a representative of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers or an authority designated by the Corps.
Wetland protection district means wetlands within the county which are indicated on the generalized wetland map. The generalized wetland map, together with all explanatory matter thereon and attached thereto, is hereby adopted by reference and declared to be a part of this article. The generalized wetland map does not represent the boundaries of jurisdictional wetlands within the county and cannot serve as a substitute for a delineation of wetland boundaries by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, as required by section 404 of the Clean Water Act, as amended. Any local government action under this article does not relieve the land owner from federal or state permitting requirements.

489:
(a) These regulations and the generalized wetland map may from time to time be amended in accordance with procedures and requirements in the general statutes and as new information concerning wetland locations, soils, hydrology, flooding or plant species peculiar to wetlands becomes available.
(b) Source wetlands map is the Fish and Wildlife Service National Wetlands Inventory maps. The county should consider the limitations of available map resources used to compile the generalized wetland map. To varying degrees, all maps contain systematic distortion and inaccuracy. Generally, inaccuracy grows larger with decreasing map scale. Commonly used wetland maps, such as the National Wetland Inventory (NWI) maps, are drawn at a scale of 1:24,000. This means that one inch on the map represents 24,000 inches on the ground, or 2,000 feet (approximately two-fifths of a mile). Maps of this scale cannot define wetland boundaries in a legally defensible way. In addition, many small and isolated wetlands may not be shown on these maps. For these reasons, the generalized wetland map adopted by the county can only be regarded as a general reference document, which may serve a variety of functions, such as indicating the need for seeking advice or a wetland determination from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. A generalized wetland map, at a scale of 1:24,000, cannot be used to delineate, in a legally defensible manner, the boundaries of jurisdictional wetlands. Formal delineation of wetlands that are protected by section 404 of the Clean Water Act, is vested with the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The Soil Conservation Service (SCS) of the U.S. Department of Agriculture is the lead agency for making wetland delineations on agricultural lands.
(Code 1996, § 34-211; Ord. of 1-23-2001(3), § 10)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Addition (to an existing building) means any walled and roofed expansion to the perimeter of a building in which the addition is connected by a common load-bearing wall other than a firewall. Any walled and roofed addition which is connected by a fire wall or is separated by an independent perimeter load-bearing wall shall be considered new construction.
Appeal means a request for a review of the county administrator's or his or her designee's interpretation of any provision of this chapter.
Area of shallow flooding means a designated AO or AH zone on a community's flood insurance rate map (FIRM) with base flood depths from one to three feet, and/or where a clearly defined channel does not exist, where the path of flooding is unpredictable and indeterminate, and where velocity flow may be evident.
Area of special flood hazard means the land in the floodplain within a community subject to a one percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year. In the absence of official designation by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, areas of special flood hazard shall be those designated by the local community and referenced in section 20-59.
Base flood means the flood having a one percent chance of being equaled or exceeded in any given year.
Basement means that portion of a building having its floor subgrade (below ground level) on all sides.
Building means any structure built for support, shelter, or enclosure for any occupancy or storage.
Development means any man-made change to improved or unimproved real estate, including, but not limited to, buildings or other structures, mining, dredging, filling, grading, paving, excavating, drilling operations, and permanent storage of materials or equipment.
Elevated building means a non-basement building built to have the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area elevated above the ground level by means of fill, solid foundation perimeter walls, pilings, columns, piers, or shear walls adequately anchored so as not to impair the structural integrity of the building during a base flood event.
Existing construction means any structure for which the start of construction commenced before the date a flood hazard boundary map is approved by the board of commissioners.
Existing manufactured home park or subdivision means a manufactured home park or subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including, at a minimum, the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is completed before the date a flood hazard boundary map is approved by the board of commissioners.
Expansion to an existing manufactured home park or subdivision means the preparation of additional sites by the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads).
Flood or flooding means a general and temporary condition of partial or complete inundation of normally dry land areas from:
(1) The overflow of inland or tidal waters; or
(2) The unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters from any source.
Flood hazard boundary map (FHBM) means an official map of a community, issued by the Federal Insurance Administration, where the boundaries of areas of special flood hazard have been defined as Zone A.
Flood insurance rate map (FIRM) means an official map of a community, issued by the Federal Insurance Administration, delineating the areas of special flood hazard and/or risk premium zones applicable to the community.
Flood insurance study (FIS) means the official report by the Federal Insurance Administration evaluating flood hazards and containing flood profiles and water surface elevations of the base flood.
Floodplain means any land area susceptible to flooding.
Floodway means the channel of a river or other watercourse and the adjacent land areas that must be reserved in order to discharge the base flood without cumulatively increasing the water surface elevation more than a designated height.
Highest adjacent grade means the highest natural elevation of the ground surface, prior to construction, adjacent to the proposed foundation of a building.
Historic structure means any structure that is:
(1) Listed individually in the National Register of Historic Places (a listing maintained by the U.S. Department of the Interior) or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the Interior as meeting the requirements for individual listing on the National Register;
(2) Certified or preliminarily determined by the Secretary of the Interior as contributing to the historical significance of a registered historic district or a district preliminarily determined by the Secretary to qualify as a registered historic district;
(3) Individually listed on a state inventory of historic places and determined as eligible by states with historic preservation programs which have been approved by the Secretary of the Interior; or
(4) Individually listed on a local inventory of historic places and determined as eligible by communities with historic preservation programs that have been certified either:
a. By an approved state program as determined by the Secretary of the Interior; or
b. Directly by the Secretary of the Interior in states without approved programs.
Lowest floor means the lowest floor of the lowest enclosed area, including basement. An unfinished or flood resistant enclosure, used solely for parking of vehicles, building access, or storage, in an area other than a basement, is not considered a building's lowest floor, provided that such enclosure is not built so as to render the structure in violation of other provisions of this Code.
Manufactured home means a building, transportable in one or more sections, built on a permanent chassis and designed to be used with or without a permanent foundation when connected to the required utilities. The term "manufactured home" also includes park trailers, travel trailers, and similar transportable structures placed on a site for 180 consecutive days or longer and intended to be improved property.
Mean sea level means the average height of the sea for all stages of the tide. It is used as a reference for establishing various elevations within the floodplain. The term "mean sea level" is synonymous with National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD).
National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) means the National Geodetic Vertical Datum (NGVD) as corrected in 1929, and is a vertical control used as a reference for establishing varying elevations within the floodplain.
New construction means any structure (see Structure) for which the start of construction commenced after the date a flood hazard boundary map is approved by the board of commissioners and includes any subsequent improvements to the structure.
New manufactured home park or subdivision means a manufactured home park or subdivision for which the construction of facilities for servicing the lots on which the manufactured homes are to be affixed (including, at a minimum, the installation of utilities, the construction of streets, and either final site grading or the pouring of concrete pads) is completed on or after the date a flood hazard boundary map is approved by the board of commissioners.
Recreational vehicle means a vehicle which is:
(1) Built on a single chassis;
(2) 400 square feet or less when measured at the largest horizontal projection;
(3) Designed to be self-propelled or permanently towable by a light-duty truck; and
(4) Designed primarily not for use as a permanent dwelling but as temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, travel, or seasonal use.

(1) The term "start of construction" means the date the development permit was issued, provided the actual start of construction, repair, reconstruction, or improvement was within 180 days of the permit date. The term "actual start" means the first placement of permanent construction of the structure such as the pouring of slabs or footings, installation of piles, construction of columns, or any work beyond the stage of excavation, and includes the placement of a manufactured home on a foundation. The term "permanent construction" does not include initial land preparation, such as clearing, grading and filling; nor does it include the installation of streets and/or walkways; nor does it include excavation for a basement, footings, piers or foundations or the erection of temporary forms; nor does it include the installation on the property of buildings appurtenant to the permitted structure, such as garages or sheds not occupied as dwelling units or part of the main structure.
(2) Accessory structures are not exempt from any ordinance requirements. For a substantial improvement, the term "actual start of construction" means the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor, or other structural part of a building, whether or not that alteration affects the external dimensions of the building.
Structure means a walled and roofed building that is principally above ground, a manufactured home, or a gas or liquid storage tank.
Substantial damage means damage of any origin sustained by a structure whereby the cost of restoring the structure to its before-damaged condition would equal or exceed 50 percent of the market value of the structure before the damage occurred.
Substantial improvement.
(1) The term "substantial improvement" means any combination of repairs, reconstruction, alteration, or improvements to a building, taking place during a five-year period, in which the cumulative cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of the market value of the structure prior to the improvement. The market value of the building should be:
a. The appraised value of the structure prior to the start of the initial repair or improvement; or
b. In the case of damage, the value of the structure prior to the damage occurring.
(2) The term "substantial improvement" includes structures which have incurred substantial damage, regardless of the actual amount of repair work performed. For the purposes of this definition, substantial improvement is considered to occur when the first alteration of any wall, ceiling, floor, or other structural part of the building commences, whether or not that alteration affects the external dimensions of the building.
(3) The term "substantial improvement" does not, however, include those improvements of a building required to comply with existing health, sanitary, or safety code specifications which are solely necessary to ensure safe living conditions, which have been pre-identified by the code enforcement official, and not solely triggered by an improvement or repair project.
Substantially improved existing manufactured home park or subdivision means an existing manufactured home park or subdivision in which the repair, reconstruction, rehabilitation or improvement of the streets, utilities and pads equals or exceeds 50 percent of the value of the streets, utilities and pads before the repair, reconstruction or improvement commenced.
Variance means a grant of relief from the requirements of this chapter which permits construction in a manner otherwise prohibited by this chapter.

In all areas of special flood hazard, the following provisions are required:
(1) New construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement of the structure.
(2) New construction and substantial improvements of existing structures shall be constructed with materials and utility equipment resistant to flood damage.
(3) New construction or substantial improvements of existing structures shall be constructed by methods and practices that minimize flood damage.
(4) Elevated buildings. All new construction or substantial improvements of existing structures that include any fully enclosed area located below the lowest floor formed by foundation and other exterior walls shall be designed so as to be an unfinished or flood-resistant enclosure. The enclosure shall be designed to equalize hydrostatic flood forces on exterior walls by allowing for the automatic entry and exit of floodwater.
a. Designs for complying with this requirement must either be certified by a professional engineer or architect or meet the following minimum criteria:
1. Provide a minimum of two openings having a total net area of not less than one square inch for every square foot of enclosed area subject to flooding;
2. The bottom of all openings shall be no higher than one foot above grade; and
3. Openings may be equipped with screens, louvers, valves or other coverings or devices provided they permit the automatic flow of floodwater in both directions.
b. So as not to violate the lowest floor criteria of this article, the unfinished or flood-resistant enclosure shall only be used for parking of vehicles, limited storage of maintenance equipment used in connection with the premises, or entry to the elevated area.
c. The interior portion of such enclosed area shall not be partitioned or finished into separate rooms.
(5) All heating and air conditioning equipment and components, all electrical, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities shall be designed and/or located so as to prevent water from entering or accumulating within the components during conditions of flooding.
(6) Manufactured homes shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse, or lateral movement. Methods of anchoring may include, but are not limited to, use of over-the-top or frame ties to ground anchors. This standard shall be in addition to and consistent with applicable state requirements for resisting wind forces.
(7) New and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the system.
(8) New and replacement sanitary sewage systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the systems and discharges from the systems into floodwaters.
(9) On-site waste disposal systems shall be located and constructed to avoid impairment to them or contamination from them during flooding.
(10) Any alteration, repair, reconstruction or improvement to a structure which is not compliant with the provisions of this chapter shall be undertaken only if the nonconformity is not furthered, extended or replaced.

(1) New construction and substantial improvements. Where base flood elevation data are available, new construction or substantial improvement of any structure or manufactured home shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation. Should solid foundation perimeter walls be used to elevate a structure, openings sufficient to facilitate the unimpeded movements of floodwaters shall be provided in accordance with standards of section 20-111(4), concerning elevated buildings.
(2) Nonresidential construction. New construction or the substantial improvement of any structure located in A1-30, AE, or AH zone may be floodproofed in lieu of elevation. The structure, together with attendant utility and sanitary facilities, must be designed to be watertight to one foot above the base flood elevation, with walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water, and structural components having the capability of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and the effect of buoyancy. A registered professional engineer or architect shall certify that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted standards of practice for meeting the provisions above and shall provide such certification to the official as set forth above and in section 20-91(6).
(3) Manufactured homes and recreational vehicles. Where base flood elevation data are available:
a. All manufactured homes placed or substantially improved on:
1. Individual lots or parcels;
2. In new or substantially improved manufactured home parks or subdivisions;
3. In expansions to existing manufactured home parks or subdivisions; or
4. On a site in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision where a manufactured home has incurred substantial damage as the result of a flood;
must have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one foot above the base flood elevation.
b. Manufactured homes placed or substantially improved in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision may be elevated so that either:
1. The lowest floor of the manufactured home is elevated no lower than one foot above the level of the base flood elevation; or
2. The manufactured home chassis is elevated and supported by reinforced piers (or other foundation elements of at least an equivalent strength) of no less than 36 inches in height above grade.
c. All manufactured homes must be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation system to resist flotation, collapse and lateral movement. See section 20-111(6).
d. All recreational vehicles placed on sites must either:
1. Be fully licensed and ready for highway use (a recreational vehicle is ready for highway use if it is licensed, on its wheels or jacking system, attached to the site only by quick disconnect type utilities and security devices, and has no permanently attached structures or additions); or
2. Meet all the requirements for new construction, including the anchoring and elevation requirements of article IV of this chapter.
(4) Floodway. Located within areas of special flood hazard established in article III of this chapter are areas designated as floodway. A floodway may be an extremely hazardous area due to velocity floodwaters, debris or erosion potential. a. Encroachments are prohibited, including earthen fill, new construction, substantial improvements or other development within the regulatory floodway. Development may be permitted however, provided it is demonstrated through hydrologic and hydraulic analyses performed in accordance with standard engineering practice that the encroachment shall not result in any increase in flood levels or floodway widths during a base flood discharge. A registered professional engineer must provide supporting technical data and certification thereof.
b. Only if this article is satisfied, then any new construction or substantial improvement shall comply with all other applicable flood hazard reduction provisions of this article.

(6) State Route 368.

(a) Truck routes mandatory. All through trucks are required to travel upon designated truck routes. All other trucks are required to travel upon truck routes, except in any of the following limited circumstances:
(1) Local pickups and deliveries. If the terminal, point of origin, or place of pickup or delivery of the truck is not located on a designated truck route, then the vehicle may travel on non-truck routes only by the shortest, most direct route between such places and the nearest designated truck route. Trucks shall not use any restricted roads, unless the origination or destination of the truck is on a restricted road, in which case, the truck shall travel by the shortest, most direct route between the nearest truck route then the nearest non-truck route to or from the origination/destination. The route requiring the fewest miles of travel shall be considered the shortest, most direct route;
(2) Non-truck route special use permit. If a non-truck route special use permit is obtained from the county for the truck, prior to travel on any non-truck routes, the truck may travel on those non-truck routes and restricted roads specifically identified in the permit for the duration of the permit;
(b) Proof of origination or destination. There shall be a presumption that the permissible place of pickup or delivery of a truck found to be on a restricted road is not located on a restricted road, unless the driver of the truck present to a law enforcement officers, at the time of the stop of said truck by law enforcement officers, written evidence of destination and point of origin, such as a log book, weight slips, delivery slips, bill of lading, or other written evidence of destination and point of origin to justify the presence of the truck on a county road other than a truck route.
(c) Bridges. Notwithstanding any provision of this section, no truck or vehicle of any kind shall be operated over a county bridge with a posted limit less than the total gross weight of the truck or vehicle and its load.
(d) Temporary closures. If any designated truck route, or portion thereof, shall be under repair or otherwise temporarily out of use, trucks shall use such other temporary route as may be designated by the state or county.
(e) Penalties for violation. Violation of any part of this section shall be punishable in accordance with the provisions on section 1-12. Violation of subsection (a) of this section shall subject the violating operator of a truck or restricted motor vehicle, to the following penalties:
(1) First offense: $125.00.
(2) Second offense within 24 months: $500.00.
(3) Third or subsequent offense within 24 months: $500.00 and up to 60 days in jail.
(f) Unladen trucks. Trucks that are not hauling a load or any portion of a load are not required to travel upon designated truck routes. However, unladen trucks shall not travel upon roads which are marked "No Through Trucks," unless they are in compliance with the provisions of subsection (a)(1) of this section.
(Ord of 7-13-2009, § 1(58-71); Ord. of 10-19-2009, §§ 3, 4)
576:
(a) Permit. The owner or operator of trucks or restricted motor vehicles may apply for a permit, allowing for limited travel on certain designated non-truck routes and restricted roads, for purposes of accessing restricted roads during the course of a construction project of limited duration requiring access by a truck on and over restricted roads.
(b) Application. An application for non-truck route special use permit may be made upon a form provided by the county. In addition to any information required in the application, an applicant must provide a highlighted map of the proposed route, which may be rejected or accepted in whole, or in part, or modified. The application fee for such a permit shall be as determined by the board of commissioners, and must be paid prior to consideration of any application.
(c) Standards for approval. Upon receipt of a complete application, the board of commissioners, or its designee, may grant or deny the application in its sole discretion based upon whether granting or denying the application is in the best interests of the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the county.
(d) Permit requirements. In addition to any other restrictions set forth in the application, upon the granting of an application, a permit holder must comply with the following conditions:
(1) All vehicles, loaded and unloaded, must stay on the route approved by the county or its designee.
(2) All vehicles must obey all traffic laws and all other provisions of this Code.
(3) All drivers must carry a copy of the approved special use permit and route map in the vehicle at all times.
(4) All drivers must have a bill of lading or other proof stating the destination and weight of the load.
(5) The permit holder must procure a surety bond or irrevocable letter of credit protecting the county against damage caused by the use of restricted roads. The surety bond shall be executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in the state and shall be in the amount of $5,000.00. The irrevocable letter of credit shall be issued by a bank or savings and loan association as defined by state law and shall be in the amount of $5,000.00.
(e) Duration. A permit issued under this section is valid for 30 days from issuance, or until all travel on non-truck routes pursuant to the permit is complete, whichever is shorter. Permits may be renewed for an additional 30 days upon the submission and approval of a new application and payment of an additional application fee.
(f) Penalties for violation. Any violation of this section shall be punishable in accordance with the provisions in section 1-12. Any non-approved deviation from the routes specified in the non-truck route special use permit shall subject the violator to the penalties set forth in section 1-12. In addition to any fine or imprisonment for violation of this section, the violation of any provision of this section, or the failure of the permit holder or anyone on its behalf to adhere to all requirements of the permit, may result in the revocation of the permit by the county.
(g) Damage to roads. If any permit holder damages county roads due to its activities under this section, whether in compliance with or in violation of, such permit holder shall be liable to the county for the actual damage to county roads caused by permit holder, as well as consequential damages.
(h) Revocation.
(1) The board of commissioners, or its designee, may revoke any permit issued under this section based upon any of the following:
a. The violation of any provisions of this section;
b. The failure to comply with any requirements of this section;
c. The violation of any other ordinances, regulations, or laws; or
d. For any actions or inactions by the permit holder deemed in the sole discretion of the county, or its designee, to be harmful to the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the county.
(2) Revocation shall become effective upon the sending of written notice by the county to the permit holder. The decision to revoke a permit under this subsection (h) rests solely in the discretion of the county or its designee.

(a) Generated waste by households or businesses. The convenience centers shall only be used for the disposal of household waste generated in private homes. Waste generated in or by the operation of any business or industry, including, but not limited to, construction or demolition activities, and any other waste not specifically allowed herein, shall not be disposed of at the convenience centers, but may be disposed of at the solid waste transfer station unless otherwise prohibited.

(1) Glass. Only beverage containers of either clear, brown/amber, or green glass may be disposed of in the designated glass recycling containers. Glass recyclables must be separated by color. The following glass items may not be disposed of in the glass recycling containers: drinking glasses, window glass, Pyrex or Visions-type cookware, light bulbs, ceramic items, and similar items.
(2) Aluminum. Only aluminum beverage cans may be disposed of in the designated aluminum recycling containers. The following metal items may not be disposed of in the aluminum recycling containers: steel or tin food cans.
(3) Plastic. Only empty milk jugs, water jugs, juice jugs, and soda bottles marked with recycling code #1 or #2 may be disposed of in the designated plastic recycling containers. The following plastic items may not be disposed of in the plastic recycling containers: motor oil containers, butter tubs, plastic bags, foam, plastic cups, or plastic plates.
(4) Newspapers. Only clean, dry, untied and unbagged newspapers and newspaper inserts may be disposed of in the designated newspaper recycling containers. The following paper items may not be disposed of in the newspaper recycling containers: telephone books, cardboard, hardbound books, or magazines.
(5) Magazines. Only magazines may be disposed of in the designated magazine recycling containers. The following paper items may not be disposed of in the magazine recycling containers: telephone books, cardboard, hardbound books, or newspapers.
(6) Cardboard. Only clean and dry cardboard or poster board may be disposed of in the designated cardboard recycling containers. Cardboard boxes must be broken down to conserve space before being placed in the cardboard recycling containers. The following cardboard items may not be disposed of in the cardboard recycling containers: wax-coated or plastic-lined cardboard boxes.
(7) Scrap metal. Only dishwashers, stoves, water heaters, washing machines, refrigerators, and other non-prohibited scrap metal items may be disposed of in the designated scrap metal recycling containers. The following metal items may not be disposed of in the scrap metal recycling containers: metal cans, drums containing any liquid (such as oil, gas, paint, or chemicals), or wire.

Only chairs, sofas, mattresses, televisions, plastic swimming pools, large children toys, Styrofoam, products used for packing, garden hoses, mops and brooms, florescent bulbs, and household furniture (inside and outside) may be disposed of in the designated bulk waste recycling containers. No commercial dumping is allowed. The following items may not be disposed of in the bulk waste containers: any item that will fit in a county blue bag, construction and demolition waste, carpet, grass clippings, brush, leaves, limbs, tin, cans, or tires.
(d) Users encouraged to recycle. Users of the county transfer station and convenience centers are encouraged to recycle their waste when at all practical.
(e) Enforcement. This section shall be enforced by the county code enforcement officer or his designee, and violators shall be punished pursuant to the provisions of section 1-12.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a landfill, waste disposal area, or waste storage area intended to be used by the owner or used by others for the disposal or storage of waste without first having filed the proper application for a special use permit with the board of commissioners and having obtained such a special use permit. Comp. Mobile home subdivision. Any plot or tract of land subdivided into lots, with such lots sold or marketed, or intended to be sold or marketed, for the placement of mobile homes.
Mobile office. A prefabricated structure designed to be transported on its own wheels, flatbed, trailer or detachable wheels and used, or intended to be used, or intended to be used, or occupied for the transaction of business or the rendering of a professional service.
Open space. An area which is not used for or occupied by a driveway, off-street parking, loading space, yard or refuse storage space.
Permanent campsite. Any site where a travel trailer, camper, or recreational vehicle is set up for five or more consecutive days.
Plat. A map, plan, or layout of a county, city, town, section, subdivision, or development indicating the location and boundaries of properties, prepared by a land surveyor licensed in the state.
Pre-owned manufactured home means any manufactured home that has been previously used as a residential dwelling and has been titled.
Principal use. The primary purpose for which land or a building is used.
Right-of-way line. The dividing line between a lot, tract or parcel of land and a contiguous public right-of-way.
Travel trailer. A vehicular type unit primarily designed as temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, or travel use which either has its own motive power or is mounted on or towed by another vehicle; provided, however, that for purposes of this article, such term shall not include a "mobile home" as defined in this section. For purposes of this article, units commonly known as "trailers," "campers," "motor homes," and "recreational vehicles" ("RVs") shall be considered "travel trailers."
Travel trailer park. Any plot or tract of land on which two or more travel trailers are located or intended to be located.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-6-2008, §1; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-11))
667:
No mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer shall be used for overnight occupancy in any place, public or private, unless such mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer is manufactured in accordance with applicable law and is installed in accordance with this article and the requirements of article IV of this appendix. Any travel trailer that is set up on a permanent campsite shall comply with the provisions of this article where specified and the provisions of section 34-19 of the Elbert County Code of Ordinances and the requirements of article IV of this appendix.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-20))
668:
In all of the unincorporated areas of Elbert County, a mobile home or manufactured home, as defined in section 38-11, shall be subject to the following conditions:
(1) All mobile homes, manufactured homes and travel trailers shall be installed in strict compliance with the applicable manufacturer's installation instructions and this article. If such manufacturer's installation instructions are not explicit, not stipulated or need clarification, or when the instructions indicate that a particular requirement may be left to the authority having jurisdiction, then the installation shall be installed in strict compliance with this article and the installation standards set forth in Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 120-3-7-.14 or otherwise promulgated pursuant to the Uniform Standards Code for Manufactured Homes Act, O.C.G.A. § 8-2-130 et seq., and subsequent amendments thereto, and pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 8-2-161(2).
(2) The mobile home unit shall have a border which surrounds all of the exterior walls completely enclosing the undercarriage or underside area of the mobile home. The border material shall consist of concrete block, brick, wood, composition board or metal skirting or some similar type material. The border or skirting shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 120-3-7-.14.
(3) The mobile home or manufactured home shall have a landing or porch, with secured steps at each entrance, all of which shall comply with Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 120-3-7-.14.
(4) The mobile home shall have a supporting foundation as required by Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 120-3-7-.14.
(5) All mobile homes, manufactured homes and travel trailers shall provide for a healthful environment, with living service facilities arranged and equipped to ensure such a condition.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-21))
669:
(a) Mobile homes, manufactured homes and travel trailers shall be connected to water and sewage as provided in Ga. Comp. Rules and Regs. R. 120-3-7-.14.
(b) Utility services such as public water, gas, electricity, sewer, etc., shall not be provided to any mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer until the requirements of this article are met.
(c) All mobile homes, manufactured homes and travel trailers in the county must be served by a water and a sewer system approved by the county health department.
(d) The electric meter and service disconnect may be mounted directly to a permanently sited mobile home. A permanently sited mobile home is defined as a unit that is attached, as required by the Georgia State (Standard) Building Code, to a foundation that is constructed in accordance with the requirements of chapters 12 and 13 of the Georgia State (Standard) Building Code, and is assessed for tax purposes as real property. If the unit does not meet the above criteria, the electric meter and service disconnect shall not be mounted directly to the mobile home or travel trailer but shall be mounted on a pole or other suitable object as required by the Georgia State (Standard) Building Code.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-22))
670:
(a) Mobile homes, manufactured homes or travel trailers must be placed on a lot or parcel of land which complies with the requirements of this article.
(b) Notwithstanding the provisions of this article, the area and dimensions of a lot shall comply with the requirements of the Elbert County Health Department in regard to water and sewer systems.
(c) No mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer shall be placed on any lot or parcel of land in any zoning district in which mobile homes, manufactured homes, or travel trailers are not permitted under section 6.04.01 or which otherwise fails to comply with any provision of article IV of this appendix.
(d) No mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer shall be placed on any lot or parcel of land unless the applicant is both the record owner of the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer and the record owner of the lot or parcel of land. As used in this section, the record owner of the lot or parcel of land shall be determined by the official real estate records maintained by the office of the clerk of the superior court of the county. As used in this section, the record owner of the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer shall be determined by a valid state-issued certificate of title to said mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer ln the event that record title to either the lot or parcel of land or to the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer is transferred to an individual or entity that is not the record owner of both, then the owner of the lot or parcel of land shall cause the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer to be moved from the lot or parcel of land within 30 days of the date of said transfer.
(e) The provisions of subsection (d) of this section shall not apply travel trailers located in travel trailer parks which have properly been permitted by county code enforcement and otherwise comply with this article and otherwise comply with all provisions of article IV of this appendix.
(f) A lot shall:
(1) Contain a minimum of 43,560 square feet (one acre);
(2) Have such open and parking spaces as are required by the provisions of this article; and
(3) Have:
(A) Frontage upon a public road or street; or
(B) Access from a public street or public road by easement.
(g) Except for:
(1) The temporary use and storage use contemplated by section 38-25;
(2) Lots containing more than two acres, which comply with the requirements of this article; and
(3) Mobile home parks or travel trailer parks which comply with the requirements of this article;
no more than one mobile home or travel trailer shall be allowed on each lot.
(h) On a lot containing two or more acres of land, the owner shall be permitted to place more than one mobile home or travel trailer on the lot. If more than one mobile home or travel trailer is placed on the lot, then each mobile home or travel trailer shall require a separate, accurately described lot. Said lot must be accurately described on a plat of survey duly recorded in the public records of the clerk of the superior court of the county. Each such lot must front on a public road or provide access by an accurately described driveway or easement as shown by plat of survey.
(i) On lots exceeding two acres in size, additional mobile homes or travel trailers shall be allowed for tenant dwellings and other uses, provided that said uses shall not be inconsistent with the mobile home park regulations or travel trailer park regulations contained herein and provided, further, that the number of said additional mobile homes or travel trailers in such areas shall not exceed the ratio of one such unit per two acres of land.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-23); Ord. of 7-12-2021(1), §§ 1, 2)
671:
(a) In no event shall any mobile home or manufactured home be located within 50 feet on any county road right-of-way or state highway right-of-way.
(b) In no event shall any travel trailer be located within 200 feet on any county road right-of-way or state highway right-of-way.
(c) In no event shall any mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer be located within 50 feet of any lot property line.
(d) In no case shall the mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer be located within 200 feet of any permanent type of building owned by another party; provided the owner of said building may waive in writing this requirement, but provided further that said distance shall be at least 50 feet.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-24))
672:
(a) A single mobile unit may be used as an office in a subdivision by the developer, temporary residence during construction of permanent residence, or for other special purposes, for a period not to exceed six months upon written approval from the county board of commissioners.
(b) One mobile home as a second and temporary accessory dwelling may be allowed on a lot provided that the following conditions are met: The additional mobile home shall qualify as a temporary elder cottage housing opportunity (ECHO) unit. Such unit shall be permitted only upon a showing that the mobile home is needed on the lot in order to enable an elderly or disabled person who suffers from some medical hardship to live in close proximity to a family member or caregiver to enable such family member or caregiver to care for the health and safety of the occupant of the ECHO unit. Such ECHO unit shall be allowed as a second mobile home on a lot on a temporary basis not to exceed one calendar year, but renewable on an annual basis for a period of one year. Upon request, the owner of such lot or ECHO unit shall provide to the county administrator or his designee suitable evidence showing medical hardship.
(c) A single mobile home may be used as a storage facility so long as all plumbing fixtures are removed from the mobile home and the mobile home complies with all other requirements of this article (except for section 38-22(a) and (c) and all other requirements of law.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-25))
673:
Travel trailers that are not occupied and not connected to utilities may be stored either:
(1) Behind the front yard building height of a building in such a manner that said travel trailer is more than 25 feet from the nearest property line and said travel trailer is not visible from a public road or from adjoining property; or
(2) Screened by plantings, walls, or a solid fence of material commonly manufactured for fencing, at least eight feet in height in such a manner that said travel trailer is more than 25 feet from the nearest property line and said travel trailer is not visible from a public road or from adjoining property.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-26))
674:
All mobile home places erected or located in the county shall be required to meet the adopted building, heating, plumbing, electrical, fire, gas, mechanical, air conditioning, and all other codes, if any, adopted by the county.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-27))
675:
Any mobile home or travel trailer brought into Elbert County or moved from one location in Elbert County to another after the ordinance from which this article is derived takes effect which does not meet the requirements in the above paragraphs shall be removed within 30 days of notice of its nonconformance from the code enforcement officer, health officials, or any other county officer vested with authority to enforce these regulations. Said notice shall be personally delivered to the occupant of the mobile home or travel trailer or posted conspicuously on the mobile home or travel trailer. Additionally, said notice shall be mailed, registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the owner of the property on which the mobile home or travel trailer is located, at the property owner's address as maintained by the county tax assessor's office. All existing mobile homes, manufactured homes or travel trailers in the county must conform to all health and safety requirements in this article,when the ordinance from which it is derived takes effect. Any mobile home or travel trailer that is not removed within 30 days of notice of its nonconformance may be removed and disposed of by the county in the same manner as for unoccupied mobile homes as provided in section 38-33, and the owner of any said mobile home or travel trailer and the owner of the land on which and said mobile home or travel trailer is situated may be tried in the magistrate court of the county as provided in section 38-51.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-28))
676:
(a) All mobile homes and travel trailer shall have a current decal, evidencing payment of state and county ad valorem taxes, conspicuously displayed.
(b) For a mobile home to be considered for taxation purposes as real property, rather than as personal property, by the county tax assessor's office, the mobile home owner must either file for homestead exemption with the county tax commissioner's office, or the mobile home owner must properly file a certificate of permanent location with the office of the clerk of the superior court of the county.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-29))
678:
Mobile home parks, as defined in this article shall adhere to the following conditions, in addition to the requirements of article IV of this appendix:
(1) The minimum area per park shall be five designated and described acres; the minimum width for the portion used for entrance and exit shall be 50 feet; and the minimum width for the portion containing mobile home spaces or stands shall be 50 feet.
(2) All mobile home parks shall contain at least ten spaces meeting the standards of this article.
(3) The minimum area for each mobile home space or stand shall be 6,000 square feet.
(4) No mobile home space or stand shall be rented for residential use of a mobile home in any such park except for periods of 30 days or more, and no mobile home shall be admitted to any park unless it can be demonstrated that it meets the requirements of any additional laws and regulations of the governing authority.
(5) In addition to meeting the above requirements, the mobile home park site plan shall be accompanied by a certificate of approval from the county health department.
(6) No mobile home shall be located within:
a. Ten feet of its individual lot line.
b. 50 feet from any exterior boundary of the mobile home park.
c. 30 feet from each other and from other buildings on the property.
d. 100 feet from any public right-of-way.
(7) A buffer strip at least 50 feet wide shall be located adjacent to each exterior property line of the mobile home park and shall not be included within any individual trailer lot.
(8) Must meet buffer and landscaping requirements as required in section 38-37.
(9) No mobile home shall be admitted into any park until at least ten lots or spaces have been approved for occupancy with this article.
(10) In no case shall any mobile home be located within 200 feet of any permanent type of building owned by another party; provided the owner of said building may waive in writing this requirement, but provided further that said distance shall be at least 50 feet.
(11) Travel trailers, campers, RVs, etc., shall not be allowed in mobile home parks. Once permitted as a mobile home park, only mobile homes are allowed unless approved by the Elbert County board of commissioners or the code enforcement officer.
(12) All lot numbers must be displayed for each site. The address number to be posted shall be in numbers or letters not less than three inches tall in a color that contrast with the background.
(13) Proposed mobile home parks meeting all the requirements of this article may be allowed in R-2 zoning districts.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-30))
679:
In every mobile home park, the following street improvements and utilities shall be planned for and provided by the developer, by installation and/or payment prior to the approval of the mobile home park:
(1) Sewer. Sanitary sewer lines, septic tanks, or other sewerage disposal system shall be in conformity with requirements of the county health department.
(2) Utilities. All utilities, except power lines and telephone lines, shall be installed underground in the shoulders of the road.
(3) Street improvements. Mobile home park street improvement widths shall be 24 feet.
(4) Base and paving. Base and paving shall meet the requirements of the department of transportation for rural roads.
(5) Linear street grades. Maximum and minimum linear street grades shall be as follows:
a. Collector streets: Not more than 12 percent.
b. Sub-collectors, lanes, and parking spaces: Not more than 15 percent.
c. No linear street grade shall be less than one-half of one percent.
(6) Storm drainage facilities.
a. A registered engineer must certify that the proposed storm drainage improvements indicated on the mobile home park plan are adequate.
b. The adequate surface drainage facilities, as certified by an engineer, shall be included in the mobile home park and so indicated on the plan.
c. Where a proposed mobile home park is traversed by a watercourse, drainageway, channel, or stream, there shall be provided a stormwater easement or drainage right-of-way along each side of the channel or course for the purpose of widening, deepening, relocating, improving, or protecting such drainage easement.
(7) Street lighting. Street lighting shall be provided throughout the park.
(8) Garbage facilities. The owner of the mobile home park shall provide an approved leak-proof container with close-fitting covers for the storage of garbage until removed from the premises for disposal. The container shall be emptied in a timely manner as to not let garbage overflow or fall onto the ground. The garbage facilities shall be adequately screened so they are not visible from any street abutting the park, any adjoining property and shall meet the setback requirements of this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-31))
680:
All mobile home subdivisions shall be required to meet all the standards and provisions of article III of this appendix.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-32))
681:
Any mobile home left unoccupied for 180 days or more, that is not being used as a storage facility as permitted in this article , shall be removed within 30 days after the owner of the land on which the mobile home is situated has been notified. Said notice shall be posted conspicuously on the mobile home. Additionally, said notice shall be mailed, registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the owner of the property on which the mobile home is located, at the property owner's address as maintained by the county tax assessor's office. If the abandoned mobile home is not removed at the end of 30 days, the county shall have said mobile home disposed of and the landowner will be charged for the removal, which said charge may be collected by the county as for collection of county ad valorem property taxes.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-33))
682:
The county shall not accept the dedication of any streets located in mobile home parks.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-34))
684:
Travel trailer parks, as defined in this article, shall adhere to the following conditions in addition to the requirements of article IV of this appendix:
(1) The minimum area per park shall be five designated and described acres in a R-2 zoning district, and the minimum area per park shall be ten designated and described acres in an A zoning district, and the location of all improvements, entrances, exits, and spaces, and streets must facilitate efficient park design, use, and management.
(2) Proposed travel trailer parks meeting all the requirements of this article may be allowed in R-2 zoning districts, and may be allowed in A zoning districts with a conditional use approval.
(3) The minimum area for each travel trailer space shall be 1,000 square feet, with a width of no less than 20 feet and a length of no less than 50 feet, with a gravel base of four inches.
(4) Each travel trailer space shall be located no closer than:
a. 20 feet of its individual lot line.
b. 50 feet from any exterior boundary of the travel trailer park.
c. 100 feet from any public right-of-way.
(5) Each travel trailer space shall have individual connection to electrical, water and sewer.
(6) Must meet buffer and landscaping requirements as required in section 38-37.
(7) In no case shall any travel trailer be located within 200 feet of any permanent type of building owned by another party; provided the owner of said building may waive in writing this requirement, but provided further that said distance shall be at least 50 feet.
(8) Mobile homes and modular homes shall not be allowed in travel trailer parks. Once permitted as a travel trailer park, only travel trailers are allowed unless approved by the county board of commissioners or the code enforcement officer.
(9) If spaces or travel trailers are rented out to members of the public, sanitary bathing facilities shall be made available for the use of park visitors. A set of bathing facilities shall be provided for each gender and for every ten travel trailer spaces. The facilities shall be connected to the park's water and sewage systems approved by the county health department and in compliance with all state regulations.
(10) Structures helpful to the operation and management of the travel trailer park, including, but not limited to, park management headquarters and laundry facilities, may be allowed, so long as building permits are obtained and the requirements of chapter 8 of the Elbert County Code of Ordinances, Buildings and Building Regulations, are met.
(11) All site plans must be approved by the code enforcement officer prior to the commencement of any construction.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-35))
685:
In every travel trailer park, the following street improvements and utilities shall be planned for and provided by the developer, by installation and/or payment prior to the approval of the travel trailer park:
(1) Sewer. Sanitary sewer lines, septic tanks, or other sewerage disposal system shall be in conformity with requirements of the county health department.
(2) Utilities. All utilities, except power lines and telephone lines, shall be installed underground in the shoulders of the road.
(3) Street improvements. Travel trailer park street improvement widths shall be 24 feet.
(4) Base and paving. Base and paving shall meet the requirements of the department of transportation for rural roads, except that paving shall not be required so long as a crush and run base is provided and is kept well maintained.
(5) Linear street grades. Maximum and minimum linear street grades shall be as follows:
a. Collector streets: Not more than 12 percent.
b. Sub-collectors, lanes, and parking spaces: Not more than 15 percent.
c. No linear street grade shall be less than one-half of one percent.
(6) Storm drainage facilities.
a. A registered engineer must certify that the proposed storm drainage improvements indicated on the travel trailer park plan are adequate.
b. The adequate surface drainage facilities, as certified by an engineer, shall be included in the travel trailer park and so indicated on the plan.
c. Where a proposed travel trailer park is traversed by a watercourse, drainageway, channel, or stream, there shall be provided a stormwater easement or drainage right-of-way along each side of the channel or course for the purpose of widening, deepening, relocating, improving, or protecting such drainage easement.
(7) Street lighting. Street lighting shall be provided throughout the park.
(8) Garbage facilities. The owner of the travel trailer park shall provide an approved leak-proof container with close-fitting covers for the storage of garbage until removed from the premises for disposal. The container shall be emptied in a timely manner as to not let garbage overflow or fall onto the ground. The garbage facilities shall be adequately screened so they are not visible from any street abutting the park or any adjoining property and shall meet the setback requirements of this article.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-36))
687:
In every mobile home park and travel trailer park, the following landscaping, buffers and screening shall be planned for and provided by the developer prior to the approval of the mobile home park or travel trailer park:
(1) The park shall have grass planted to prevent erosion and the stirring of dust. The grass shall be maintained as to not pose an eyesore or attract rodents, insects or snakes, or pose a fire hazard. All exposed soil in the development shall be covered by grass or sod prior to the issuance of a certificate of occupancy.
(2) All landscaping in the park shall be maintained so as to not pose an eyesore or attract rodents, insects or snakes, or cause a condition that is odorous or capable of causing disease or annoyance, or pose a fire hazard.
(3) All exterior property in the park shall be kept free from any accumulation of rubbish or garbage, including, but not limited to, mattresses, furniture, and tires.
(4) Buffers between the park and adjoining properties are required. Buffers shall consist of either plantings, fencing, and/or walls, in accordance with the following standards:
(a) Plantings. Plantings shall consist of trees or shrubs or a combination of the two. Planted areas shall be along the abutting property lines or in an area that provides the best screening effectiveness. Planting shall be of the type reasonably expected to attain a minimum height of eight feet and a canopy spread of ten feet within four years. If plantings are used as screening, the planting area shall have a minimum base width of 12 feet.
(b) Fencing. Fences shall be a minimum of six feet in height but not greater than eight feet. The fencing shall be constructed of standard wood fencing material or other suitable material that will provide 90 percent visual blockage. Fences shall be maintained structurally sound and in good repair.
(c) Walls. Walls shall be of masonry construction and a minimum of six feet in height but not greater than eight feet. Walls shall be maintained structurally sound and in good repair.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-37))
690:
It shall be unlawful for any person to commence the excavation for or construction of a mobile home, travel trailer, manufactured home or combination park or place a mobile home, mobile office or travel trailer on an individual lot until a building permit authorizing such action has been properly issued.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-40))
692:
Fees for building permits required under section 38-40 shall be paid by the developer or property owner according to the following schedule:
(1) Development of a mobile home park: $750.00 for the first 25 spaces, plus an additional $30.00 for each mobile home space thereafter; and
(2) Development of a travel trailer park: $500.00 for the first 25 spaces, plus an additional $20.00 for each travel trailer space thereafter.
(3) Each travel trailer shall be permitted at a $50.00 fee, license plates must be valid and current and inspections are required to ensure proper hookups. Each travel trailer that meets the permanent campsite definition, shall per permitted each year and proof of current tags shall be submitted to obtain a permit.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-42))
693:
No mobile home or office on an individual lot and no mobile home, travel trailer or manufactured home shall be occupied or used until after the commissioners or designated agent shall have issued a certificate of occupancy therefor. This certificate shall be evidence that requirements of this article have been met.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-43))
694:
(a) The board of commissioners shall have the authority to issue a temporary permit allowing a mobile home or travel trailer to be placed on an individual lot for nonresidential use where the applicant for such permit shows that it is necessary to use such mobile home, manufactured home or travel trailer as an office or work area for the preparation and completion of a construction project. Such permit shall expire one year from the date of issue or upon completion of the project, whichever first occurs, and may be renewed once.
(b) The board may issue a temporary permit allowing mobile home or travel trailer to be placed on a residential lot for residential purposes when the applicant for such permit first shows:
(1) Special circumstances or existing conditions are such that the denial of such permit would deprive the applicant of any reasonable or beneficial use of his land (mere loss in value will not justify approval), or that the denial of such permit would cause an undue hardship or burden on the applicant to the extent that a denial would be injurious to the applicant's physical well-being;
(2) The granting of such permit shall not be injurious to the neighborhood or detrimental to the public welfare; and
(3) Adequate facilities are available for water and sewerage.
(c) Any such permit issued pursuant to subsection (b) of this section shall expire one year from the date of issue, and may be renewed only by following the procedures governing its original issue.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-44))
695:
Prior to the beginning of the development of a mobile home park or travel trailer park, the developer shall comply with this article and section 34-19 of the Elbert County Code of Ordinances, as well as other applicable sections of this Code.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-45))
696:
A permit shall be required to locate a pre-owned manufactured home in the jurisdiction.
(a) Permit. To obtain a permit, applicants shall provide to the building inspector:
(1) An affidavit signed by the applicant that the pre-owned manufactured home meets health and safety standards required by this Act.
(2) Photographs of the interior and exterior of the pre-owned manufactured home providing evidence that home meets the minimum health and safety standards.
(3) A $50.00 refundable guarantee of condition bond or $50.00 refundable cash deposit.
(4) The guarantee of condition bond or cash deposit will be forfeited after 90 days from the date of inspection, unless all conditions and standards are met prior to the end of the 90 days or an extension has been issued in writing by the building inspector.
(5) The permit and inspection fee required by subsection (d) of this section.
(6) A photocopy of the septic tank permit issued by the county environmental health office.
(7) Proof of payment of county ad valorem taxes to date.
(8) Proof of transfer of title in the office of the county tax commissioner's office if said mobile home is not purchased new, and a copy of the bill of sale if said mobile home is purchased new.
(9) A photocopy of a properly recorded deed and plat to the lot or parcel on which the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer will be located.
(10) A photocopy of a state-issue certificate of title to the mobile home, manufactured home, or travel trailer.
(b) Inspection. Upon receipt of a permit, applicants may relocate the manufactured home on a residential site for the purposes of inspection. Applicants shall arrange for an inspection to be held once the installation of the manufactured home is complete.
(c) Certificate of occupancy. A certificate of occupancy shall be issued to the applicant at such time that the building inspector certifies that the requirements of this article have been met.
(d) Fee. A permit and inspection fee of $50.00 shall be charged to the applicant to cover the cost to the county to process the permit application and inspect the pre-owned manufactured home. Such fee shall cover the initial inspection and one follow-up inspection. The applicant shall be charged $25.00 for each additional follow-up inspection that may be necessary. Owners of pre-owned manufactured homes that are not in compliance upon a third inspection shall have their permit revoked and shall be required to remove the home from the jurisdiction at their own expense.
(e) Alternative inspection. At the request of the applicant, the building inspector may, at his or her discretion, inspect a pre-owned manufactured home prior to its being relocated if the home is then located at another site within the county.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-46); Ord. of 7-12-2021(1), § 5)
697:
All pre-owned manufactured homes shall comply with the following before being issued a certificate of occupancy by the building inspector:
HUD Code. Every pre-owned manufactured home located in the jurisdiction shall be in compliance with the Federal Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act, 42 USC 5401—5445 (the HUD Code) and shall not have been altered in such a way that the home no longer meets the HUD Code.
Interior condition. Every floor, interior wall, and ceiling of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in sound condition. Doors and windows shall be operable, watertight and in good working condition. The floor system shall be in sound condition and free of warping, holes, water damage, or deterioration.
Exterior condition. The exterior of all pre-owned manufactured homes shall be free of loose or rotting boards or timbers and any other conditions that might admit rain or moisture to the interior portions of the walls or to occupied spaces. The exterior siding shall be free of rot and rust. Roofs shall be structurally sound and have no obvious defects that might admit rain or cause moisture to collect on the interior portion of the home.
Sanitary facilities. Every plumbing fixture, water, and waste pipe of a pre-owned manufactured home shall be in a sanitary working condition when properly connected, and shall be free from leaks and obstructions. Each home shall contain a kitchen sink. Each bathroom shall contain a lavatory and water closet. At least one bathroom shall contain a tub and/or shower facilities. Each of these fixtures shall be checked upon being connected to ensure they are in good working condition.
Heating systems. Heating shall be safe and in working condition. Unvented heaters shall be prohibited.
Electrical systems. Electrical systems (switches, receptacles, fixtures, etc.) shall be properly installed and wired and shall be in working condition. Distribution panels shall be in compliance with the approved listing, complete with required breakers, with all unused openings covered with solid covers approved and listed for that purpose. The home shall be subject to an electrical continuity test to ensure that all metallic parts are properly bonded. Each pre-owned manufactured home shall contain a water heater in safe and working order.
Hot water supply. Each home shall contain a water heater in safe and working condition.
Egress windows. Each bedroom of a manufactured home shall have at least one operable window of sufficient size to allow egress if necessary.
Ventilation. The kitchen in the home shall have at least one operating window or other ventilation device.
Smoke detectors. Each pre-owned manufactured home shall contain one operable battery-powered smoke detector in each bedroom and in the kitchen, which must be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
(Ord. of 6-7-2004; Ord. of 10-13-2020, exh. A(38-47))
